history: To be riche was first to be powerful. The Frankish word *rīki meant ‘powerful’, and in the oldest French texts, such as the Life of Saint Alexis around 1050, a riche hom is a man of power and great estates. According to the TLFi, the plain sense ‘who owns property’ is only secure from about 1265. In a world where land meant power, the two ideas were never far apart. The same Germanic word lives on in German reich and English rich, and the Romance languages took it too: Italian ricco, Spanish and Portuguese rico. The TLFi mentions a proposal that it came into Latin through Gothic. In French the family includes s'enrichir, ‘to get rich’.
historyEinfach: Riche comes from Frankish, the language of the Franks. Their word riki meant ‘powerful’. In old French, a riche man was a man with power and a lot of land. Later the word meant ‘with a lot of money’. English rich and German reich are related. Spanish says rico.

elsewhere.text: English inherited the word from its own Germanic past, so rich is a cousin of riche, not a loan from French.
